capabilities: Open or create periodic notes by clicking calendar cells
Navigate day, week, month, quarter, semester and year notes from one view
Shade cells as a heatmap from sources like word count and tags
Navigate the calendar with the keyboard
Register custom sources through a public API
extras: Full user guide, settings reference and API docs are hosted separately; requires Obsidian 1.10 or later; deliberately keeps CSS class names compatible with the Calendar plugin so existing CSS snippets keep working; installable via BRAT for pre-release testing.
intentEvidence: It is MIT licensed, and this is a reimplementation rather than a fork.
motivation: The author rewrote the Calendar plugin because it had been unmaintained since 2024, its UI package obsidian-calendar-ui was unmaintained since 2023, and other plugins could not contribute data sources to it.
problem: Obsidian has no calendar view for periodic notes, and the existing Calendar plugin covers only daily and weekly notes and cannot be extended by other plugins.

relations.evidence: Calendar by Liam Cain is the plugin that defined what a calendar in Obsidian's sidebar should feel like
reads the configuration you already have in core Daily notes and in the Periodic Notes plugin

summary: Sidebar calendar for daily through yearly periodic notes, with cells shaded by data from built-in and third-party sources.
